item.text: {"slug":"snap-participation-may-2026","country":"US","type":"data","title":"SNAP Participation, May 2026","question":"What will USDA FNS first report as total SNAP persons participating for May 2026 in the national monthly Persons table, not seasonally adjusted, converted to millions?","unit":"millions","pointEstimate":38.2,"ciLow":37.15,"ciHigh":39.25,"confidence":0.8,"resolutionDate":"2026-10-04","resolutionSource":"USDA Food and Nutrition Service SNAP Data Tables, national monthly Persons, Households, Benefits, and Average Monthly Benefit per Person and Household","resolutionSourceUrl":"https://www.fns.usda.gov/sites/default/files/resource-files/snap-4fymonthly-2.pdf","resolutionRule":"Resolve to the first official USDA FNS print for May 2026 total SNAP Persons in the national monthly participation table, using the not seasonally adjusted national total. Convert official persons to millions by multiplying by 0.000001, or official thousands to millions by multiplying by 0.001 if the released table is in thousands. Use the first print only; ignore later revisions unless the first print is withdrawn before publication as an official release.","dataPointId":"usda.fns.snap.persons.may_2026","historicalContext":[{"label":"Nov 2025 initial","value":40.395735},{"label":"Oct 2025 preliminary","value":41.0918},{"label":"Sep 2025","value":41.63309},{"label":"May 2025","value":42.248301},{"label":"Nov 2024","value":43.018848}],"drivers":["Recent official SNAP participation fell from 43.019 million in November 2024 to 40.396 million in November 2025.","Expanded 2025-2026 eligibility and work-requirement enforcement points to further participation losses by May 2026.","The November 2025 initial print is explicitly preliminary and subject to significant revision, so I avoid extrapolating its exact one-month drop mechanically.","Economic need and food-price pressure limit the downside because eligible households still have strong demand for benefits.","State implementation timing creates wide uncertainty around the May 2026 first print."],"sourceContext":["https://www.fns.usda.gov/pd/supplemental-nutrition-assistance-program-snap","https://www.fns.usda.gov/sites/default/files/resource-files/snap-4fymonthly-2.pdf","https://www.fns.usda.gov/sites/default/files/resource-files/snap-persons-2.pdf","https://www.fns.usda.gov/sites/default/files/resource-files/snap-annualsummary-2.pdf","https://apnews.com/article/4e9016f6919a603cb7d35b9c9fcb9048"],"runAt":"2026-07-10T04:17:17Z","reasoning":[{"kind":"heading","text":"USDA FNS SNAP persons forecast for May 2026"},{"kind":"text","text":"Framing and exact resolver: this is the USDA FNS SNAP national monthly Persons series, not state detail, not annual QC, not benefits paid, and not seasonally adjusted. The target unit is millions and the resolver is first print; the official table currently labels FY 2026 values as preliminary and subject to revision, so this forecast targets the first May 2026 print rather than later revised values."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Opened USDA FNS SNAP Data Tables page and national monthly SNAP PDF.","result":"Fetched official national monthly values: May 2025 Persons 42,248,301; Sep 2025 Persons 41,633,090; Oct 2025 Persons 41,091,800; Nov 2025 Persons 40,395,735; FY 2026-to-date annual summary 40,743,768 persons as of data dated February 13, 2026."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Opened USDA FNS SNAP Number of Persons Participating state-level PDF for the latest available month.","result":"Fetched official latest state-detail totals: TOTAL November 2024 43,018,848; TOTAL October 2025 41,091,800; TOTAL November 2025 initial 40,395,735; November 2025 vs October 2025 percent change -1.7%; November 2025 vs November 2024 percent change -6.1%."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Opened USDA FNS SNAP annual participation and cost summary PDF.","result":"Fetched official annual average participation: FY 2023 42,177 thousand; FY 2024 41,452 thousand; FY 2025 42,126 thousand; FY 2025 average benefit per person 187.94 dollars; FY 2025 total benefits 95,007.20 million dollars."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"public.lookup","call":"Checked public reporting on 2026 SNAP policy implementation and participation pressure.","result":"Fetched public policy context with numbers: AP reported nearly 42 million Americans receive SNAP, the expanded work requirements apply to adults aged 55-64 in addition to prior groups, and CBO projected about 2.4 million fewer SNAP participants over the next decade."},{"kind":"text","text":"Release-date note: the canonical ledger target supplies an expected official release window ending 2026-10-04 for the May 2026 first print. I used that target-contract resolutionDate. Discrepancy: in the accessible FNS pages fetched here, I found official table update dates and latest-month metadata, but not a separate public FNS calendar entry naming the May 2026 SNAP release date."},{"kind":"text","text":"Base rate/reference class: for this same official national monthly Persons variant, recent month-to-month changes from Nov 2024 through Nov 2025 averaged about -0.219 million per month, with the last four official changes at -0.204, -0.541, and -0.696 million into the Oct-Nov policy/shutdown period. The base rate is therefore a declining caseload, not a flat persistence series."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: persistence prior starts from the latest official first-print national value of 40.395735 million in Nov 2025. Historical sample is the same USDA FNS national monthly Persons series from Nov 2024-Nov 2025; successive-change sigma = 0.27 million. A one-month 80% half-width is 1.28*sigma = 0.35 million; scaling six months gives about 0.35*sqrt(6) = 0.86 million. Level/momentum adjustment applies -0.8 million for continuing recent decline, policy-mechanism adjustment applies -1.1 million for expanded work requirements and immigrant eligibility tightening by spring 2026, and one-off/reporting adjustment adds -0.3 million because latest initial prints show disruption but may revise. Point = 40.396 - 0.8 - 1.1 - 0.3 = 38.196 million, rounded to 38.20. I widen the six-month 0.86 million half-width to 1.05 million because policy implementation is staggered by state and first-print reporting is volatile, yielding 37.15 to 39.25 million."},{"kind":"text","text":"Counter-considerations: upside risk would come from November 2025 being materially undercounted or revised upward before the May first print pattern, from court or state administrative delays slowing terminations, or from weaker labor-market conditions raising eligible need; those would land above the interval if participation remains over 39.25 million. Downside risk would come from faster state enforcement, large documentation failures, or additional immigrant/work-rule terminations by May; those would land below the interval if participation falls under 37.15 million. Outside the interval is most plausible if the latest official initial prints are not comparable to normal participation counts."},{"kind":"forecast","point":38.2,"ciLow":37.15,"ciHigh":39.25}]}
